title: Building an AI game master RPG with a workflow that now feels like a wish machine
author: jleechanworldai
selftext:
![img](z6yqlzui0nzh1 "Tywin iOS app: setup (left), playable scene (middle), portrait (right).")

I'm building WorldAI, a choose-your-own-adventure RPG with an AI game master. The three Tywin screenshots above show campaign setup, a portrait, and a playable scene in the iOS app.

This isn't a greenfield app. I built an iOS frontend for my existing 500K LOC desktop app. I use ChatGPT Dot to coordinate work alongside Opus, Codex and Grokbot. The latest frontier of models feels more like a magic wish machine these days.

I work on this part-time, roughly 20-30 hours a week. Around \~100 PRs daily last few weeks.

For each PR when needed I mostly read prompts, lines of code counts, and the proof/evidence now vs reviewing code. If something seems off, I interrogate the agent, ask it to explain the change, and adjust the implementation or instructions. I still define the outcome/exit criteria, check the evidence, and decide what merges for larger PRs.

My /prw workflow starts with the player action, expected result, and what must not break. I capture the real before state, have agents implement a bounded change, and run appropriate tests. Then I repeat the same journey afterward, matching the content, starting state and platform where possible. I use captioned video for interactions and paired screenshots for static changes.

An independent reviewer inspects the actual frames and supporting evidence. Failures go back for fixes and a recheck of the affected proof. The examples below are UI evidence, but I do this for non-UI backend changes too, where I interrogate the agent and sample raw requests/responses.

Example 1: The invitation pair shows a badly cropped character portrait replaced by twin dragons around a central figure, with the same text and controls. I had agents iterate until they approved the visual evidence, then I spot checked and merged.

![img](rw9bnaaxzmzh1 "Invitation artwork: before (left), after (right).")

Example 2: This one isn't a bug fix, just a brand new flow for generating an AI avatar. I told my agents to just freestyle some nice UI without a mock and it was mostly good with a few tweaks.

![img](w7ijm09zzmzh1 "Avatar generation: before (left), after (right).")

My [Building at Idea Velocity slideshow](https://docs.google.com/presentation/d/1qLdMzZaIuP9IdpTBomuOGJTAspCEJo6Esu10zWFrhm4/htmlpresent) covers the broader approach.

For other game developers using coding agents: would you merge a UI-only change without personally reading every line if it came with tests, a matched before/after demonstration and independent review? What proof would you want for gameplay changes or story/state consistency, and where would you insist on reading the implementation?
